reason: The authoritative repository wording says only that an infinite model has elementarily equivalent models of different cardinalities. It gives no quantified cardinal, language-size bound, direction, primary-source theorem/page, or conventions. The accepted intake explicitly reserves the choice among an all-admissible-cardinals statement, one unequal-cardinality witness, and separate upward/downward forms. Those propositions are not definitionally or logically equivalent without additional scope choices, so selecting mathlib's stronger all-cardinals candidate would invent or broaden the target.
unresolved_inputs: immutable primary-source edition, exact theorem/page, incorporated definitions, and errata disposition
whether 'different cardinalities' means one unequal witness, every admissible cardinal, or paired upward/downward conclusions
whether the result is elementary equivalence only or a directional elementary embedding/substructure statement
the exact language-cardinality and infinitude bounds, including equality cases
nonempty-model convention, ordered binders, cardinal universes, and lift levels

candidate_assessment.checked_type_summary: For every infinite L-structure M and cardinal kappa with aleph_0 <= kappa and the lifted language-cardinality bound, there exists a bundled L-structure N elementarily equivalent to M with #N = kappa.
candidate_assessment.non_identity_reason: The repository sentence does not state universal quantification over kappa or its two lower-bound hypotheses. The intake therefore forbids treating candidate proximity as exact statement identity.

retry_condition: An accountable source reviewer must preserve and hash an immutable primary source, select and transcribe one exact theorem with all incorporated definitions and hypotheses, dispose of errata, and independently approve its mapping to the short repository sentence. A later statement run can then freeze binder order and universes, minimize imports, elaborate and hash the exact expression, compile any credited transports, and run removed-hypothesis, changed-domain, binder-scope, and boundary mutations.
